inspection.authority_limit: Photographs control visible likeness; generated models supply no new anatomy. Finish calibration used only for surface treatment. Photo views are uncalibrated and partly occluded; human likeness remains provisional.

story.variant_decision: Sole primary; no meaningful alternative identified by source comparison. Two distinct moments suit this short story.

findings: Neet has separate fine forelegs and hindlegs, full narrow tan trunk, projecting muzzle, broad triangular ears and a tiny rump nub. Four paws are supported on the path; no duplicated or borrowed limb is visible.

Buddy has a continuous prone trunk from shoulders to rounded pelvis. Chin sits between distinct forepaws; folded hind leg and low tail belong to the same body. Ground support and occlusions are credible without a disconnected rear body.

The short torso coats are now broad smooth color shapes rather than curled or engraved hair patterns. Buddy furnishings are concentrated around muzzle, brows, pendant ears and pale leg regions. No whole-body shag volume or raised dorsal fur contour appears.

Chirag lies coherently on the bench with near forepaw at the edge, other foreleg folded and rear leg supported. Crumbs remain on the seat below his head after the samosa; no intact new snack conflicts with the scene.

Neet directs an eager open-mouth answer upward, Chirag looks tired of the lesson, and Buddy glances toward them from his chin-down pose. This clearly supports the menu joke before Buddy stands for the test. The close framing can leave other class dogs outside view.
Sunny park, bench perspective and cast shadows are coherent. No stray text, contamination, clipped foreground feet or material finish artifact found.

Buddy has an elongated continuous torso, visible rising neck, substantial legs and real clearance beneath the chest and belly. All four feet have distinct ownership and ground support; the low tapering tail is attached to the rump.

Neet preserves a full narrow torso, fine straight forelegs, bent hindlegs, large cupped triangular ears and near-flush nub. Head and raised muzzle connect naturally to the neck; no hollow waist or long tail appears.

Buddy torso consists of restrained broad dark washes without the earlier curly interior pattern. Muzzle, brow, ear and lower-leg furnishings remain regional; limited underside fringe agrees with the visible B29 grooming rather than creating a shaggy barrel. Neet body is smooth with no material long-fur silhouette.

Heather arm and hand reach continuously from the cropped upper figure to the rear of Buddy ear. Contact reads as a gentle scratch, and closed eyes plus raised head show Buddy enjoying it. Human feet and dogs share the path plane without merging.
Neet waits separately looking up with an earnest expression, complementing Buddy relaxed reward. This matches the exact scratch anchor and does not pre-empt the smaller-mango final line.

Same warm park palette and recognizable character markings connect the two pictures; no food or contradictory prop appears on the walk home. Cropped Heather remains a provisional human depiction. Paper/wash texture is unobtrusive and no material finish defect found.

complementarity: Lesson image emphasizes a public misunderstanding and three-way reactions; closing changes scale and interaction to Buddy earned affectionate reward with Heather. They do not repeat one pose or spoil the last joke.
remaining_stage: Fresh complete illustrated reading required separately; this visual verdict does not claim that reading stage complete.
